chapters.name: THE EMPTY RECEPTION
chapters.subtitle: Someone has vanished, and the night register is lying.

chapters.name: ROOM SEVENTEEN
chapters.subtitle: A false guest. An older crime. A reason to disappear.

chapters.name: THE MISSING MINUTES
chapters.subtitle: The evidence survived. So did the person who buried it.

chapters.name: BEFORE DAWN
chapters.subtitle: Find Nina. Preserve the truth. Get out.

levels.title: Restore the Terminal
levels.objective: Rotate the connectors to carry backup power from the battery to the reception terminal.

clue.title: The impossible checkout
clue.text: Room 17 was checked out at 11:18 PM using Nina’s account, despite her handwritten warning.

story_intro: 11:43 PM. Rain lashes the windows of the Mariner Motel. Nina’s shift should have ended ten minutes ago.
Her handbag, phone, and car keys are behind the empty reception desk. The office telephone rings.
You’re late. Nina’s gone home. Just lock up the desk.
She got a lift. I’ll explain tomorrow.
He hangs up. Beneath the keyboard is a folded note: “Room 17 checked out at 11:18. That’s impossible. Check the cameras.”
The terminal’s dead. Maybe the backup panel still works.
story_reveal: Power runs through the circuit. The reception monitor flickers awake.
ROOM 17 — CHECKED OUT 11:18 PM — AUTHORISED: NINA S.
Her own account? Why leave a warning about a checkout she approved?

levels.title: The Night Register
levels.objective: Arrange the physical receipts from earliest to latest to reveal the inconsistent entry.

clue.title: The unsigned receipt
clue.text: The 11:18 PM checkout for Room 17 has no guest signature. A guest in Room 12 confirms Nina was investigating false checkouts.

story_intro: A yellow alert flashes: REGISTER DOES NOT MATCH PHYSICAL RECEIPTS.
Nina always filed these in order. Someone’s moved them.
Four receipts have been pulled from the register and stuffed beneath the cash drawer.
story_reveal: The checkout receipt has Nina’s login, but no signed departure slip.
A guest knocks on the reception glass. A woman in a raincoat waits under the awning.
Is Nina working? She told me not to leave until she checked something.
Rooms that were apparently empty... but weren’t.

levels.title: The Security Cabinet
levels.objective: Slide the storage trays to open a path to the cabinet key.

clue.title: Forgotten backup
clue.text: A removable security backup drive survived even though the main recording system was tampered with.

story_intro: The security office is unlocked. A recorder stands dark behind a glass-fronted cabinet.
The key’s in the sliding tray. Someone’s jammed it shut.
Shift the trays into their numbered positions to free the lower-right compartment.
story_reveal: The cabinet opens. A removable backup drive is still connected.
Someone pulled the primary recorder, but missed this one.
A torn label on the cabinet reads: “Service access logs — keep for audit.”

levels.title: The Missing Footage
levels.objective: Reconstruct the CCTV log in chronological order.

clue.title: A second person at the desk
clue.text: The CCTV sequence places Nina in security at 11:12, while a maintenance-jacketed person operates her terminal at 11:18.

story_intro: Four camera segments survived, but their index is scrambled.
The timestamps should tell me what happened first.
The footage starts with Nina entering the security office and ends with a vehicle moving near the rear gate.
story_reveal: The reconstructed footage plays. At 11:18 someone at reception uses Nina’s still-open terminal.
Nina was in here at 11:12. Whoever checked out Room 17 wasn’t her.
The figure at reception wears a maintenance jacket, face obscured by the camera angle.
Have you been in the security office? Don’t touch the recordings. I’m coming down.

levels.title: The Tampered Reader
levels.objective: Remove the exposed fasteners in order to open the damaged access reader.

clue.title: The impossible access
clue.text: The service corridor was opened at 11:26 PM using a NIGHT SHIFT credential, 17 minutes before the player arrived.

story_intro: The service door reader hangs crookedly from its housing.
Someone opened this after it was sealed for maintenance.
A series of overlapping retaining plates protects the memory unit.
story_reveal: The casing falls free. Its display retains the last staff credential.
That’s the credential name on my card. But I arrived at 11:43.
A distant metallic impact echoes from the service wing.

levels.title: The Backup Recorder
levels.objective: Reconnect the recorder’s damaged power circuit.

clue.title: Nina’s last recording
clue.text: A backup audio recording captures Nina confronting an unidentified man before a struggle. Police have been notified.

story_intro: The backup recorder contains one audio track that never reached the main system.
The cable was deliberately cut. I can bypass it with the spare connectors.
The playback lights are dark; the rain suddenly seems very loud.
story_reveal: A woman’s voice crackles through the speaker. It is Nina.
You weren’t supposed to find it.
A man answers, too faintly to identify. Then a heavy thud. Silence.
Nina didn’t go home. I’m calling the police.
Dispatch takes the report, but flooding has blocked the coastal road. Help is on its way.

levels.title: The Last Image
levels.objective: Slide the damaged image fragments back into their correct positions.

clue.title: Two figures in the van
clue.text: At 11:34 PM, a grey van with registration ending 61 moved toward the rear gate. Two occupants were visible.

story_intro: One final still from the rear camera is broken into digital blocks.
I need to see who was in that van.
An outline of the vehicle can be made out between scrambled strips.
story_reveal: The restored image shows a grey van at 11:34 PM. There are two silhouettes in the cabin.
One is driving. The other is slumped in the passenger seat.
The van’s registration ends in 61. The south gate camera is conveniently missing.

levels.title: The Contradiction
levels.objective: Match each recorded event to the evidence that proves it happened.

clue.title: A cloned identity
clue.text: The NIGHT SHIFT credential is assigned to the player, yet it was used before arrival and again while the player remained in the security office.

story_intro: The evidence no longer fits Owen’s story. You pin the most important findings beside the security monitor.
The timing matters. There has to be a connection.
Match each event to its supporting record.
story_reveal: The case timeline updates. The NIGHT SHIFT credential used at 11:26 is assigned to you.
But my card is in my pocket...
The security monitor chimes: ACCESS GRANTED — ROOM 17 — 12:09 AM.
Someone just used my card again.
Outside the security office, the corridor light goes out.

levels.title: Through the Door
levels.objective: Enter the four-digit room override Nina encoded in her note.

clue.title: Room 17 was staged
clue.text: Room 17 was cleaned recently, although its recorded guest never slept there. The guest name is Martin Hale.

story_intro: 12:13 AM. The passage to Room 17 is empty. The guest’s keycard slot is sealed.
Nina underlined two parts of her note: “Room 17” and “11:18”.
A pencilled instruction appears on the back: “Room + checkout minutes”.
story_reveal: The lock releases. Room 17 smells of fresh cleaning fluid, but the bathroom is still damp.
The motel’s guest welcome card bears the name MARTIN HALE. The bed has not been slept in.

levels.title: The Hidden Vent
levels.objective: Open the vent Nina marked without damaging the contents.

clue.title: The WARD memory card
clue.text: Nina hid a microSD card marked “WARD — 18 OCT 2019” in Room 17’s ventilation duct.

story_intro: A pale scratch beneath the windowsill forms a tiny arrow pointing to an air vent.
Nina left another mark. She wanted somebody to find this.
The vent cover has overlapping screws and a delicate latch.
story_reveal: Behind the vent is a waterproof sleeve containing a microSD card.
Why would a six-year-old incident be hidden in a motel room?
A vehicle engine idles outside. It stops when you look through the curtain.

levels.title: The Guest of Record
levels.objective: Match the names on motel documents with the records that connect them.

clue.title: A false guest identity
clue.text: The Room 17 booking under Martin Hale was paid for by Daniel Price’s security company.

story_intro: Three names keep appearing on the paperwork: Martin Hale, Daniel Price and Claire Bennett.
I need to know which records belong together.
Receipts, contractor invoices and a booking slip are scattered across the desk.
story_reveal: Martin Hale’s room charge was paid with a card belonging to PRICE SECURITY SERVICES.
Daniel Price. The contractor who fitted the motel’s access readers.
Room 12 was paid in cash by Claire Bennett, who specifically asked about Room 17.

levels.title: The Vehicle Trace
levels.objective: Use the yard movement model to clear a route for the grey van.

clue.title: The van never left
clue.text: The grey van likely returned to the motel’s hidden loading bay rather than departing through the chained south gate.

story_intro: The yard camera cannot show the south gate. It can show where all the parked vehicles were.
If I reconstruct the available route, I’ll know whether the van could have left.
On the security map, select a vehicle and use the arrows to slide it within its lane.
story_reveal: With the yard layout reconstructed, the van’s supposed exit route makes no sense.
It could reach the south lane, but the gate was chained. It must have doubled back.
The back of the site contains a loading bay obscured from both main cameras.

levels.title: The Dashcam Fragment
levels.objective: Restore the obscured still from the van’s own camera.

clue.title: The rear-laundry turn
clue.text: A dashcam fragment places the grey van near the rear laundry entrance at 11:36 PM.

story_intro: A dashcam sync station in the loading bay contains a partial image from 11:36 PM.
The van’s own camera caught the turn.
The corrupted still breaks into fragments whenever it loads.
story_reveal: The repaired frame shows the van turning left behind the laundry block.
A chained corridor leads from the loading bay to the disused service wing.

levels.title: The Ward File
levels.objective: Sort the incident documents into the order they were created.

clue.title: Mara Ward’s death
clue.text: Mara Ward was killed in a 2019 hit-and-run. Claire Bennett is her sister, Claire Ward, investigating the disappearance of evidence.

story_intro: The microSD card holds scans of a police report, an insurance claim and motel maintenance notes.
They’re all about someone called Mara Ward.
Arrange the documents by date to uncover what was filed—and what was changed.
story_reveal: Mara Ward died following a hit-and-run on the coastal road on 18 October 2019.
My name is Claire Ward. Mara was my sister.
You checked in under another name?
I tried using my own name once. Someone warned me to stop asking questions.
Nina contacted Claire after discovering an old security archive.

levels.title: The Sealed Recording
levels.objective: Open the evidence archive using the incident year.

clue.title: The cover-up recording
clue.text: A 2019 recording implicates Owen Mercer and Daniel Price in suppressing evidence of Mara Ward’s death. A weak intercom call suggests Nina is alive.

story_intro: The card includes a locked audio archive marked WARD / INCIDENT YEAR.
Nina said she had proof the motel knew what happened.
The code prompt says four-digit incident year.
story_reveal: I changed the insurance paperwork, Daniel. You told me nobody was hurt.
Keep the camera logs where they are, Owen. Nobody needs to see the road.
Owen helped conceal the old collision. But the recording doesn’t prove who was driving.
A crackle comes through the building intercom. A faint female voice says, “...laundry... please...”
Nina’s alive. Somewhere behind the service wing.

levels.title: The Spare Credential
levels.objective: Connect the access events to the staff and maintenance credentials.

clue.title: Who copied the card
clue.text: A contractor tool assigned to Daniel Price’s company duplicated the NIGHT SHIFT credential at 10:57 PM.

story_intro: Daniel Price installed the motel’s new electronic readers last month.
He could have made a second card with the same identifier.
The contractor audit lists three cards and their associated authorisations.
story_reveal: The NIGHT SHIFT identifier was duplicated by a contractor tool at 10:57 PM.
That explains why it registered before I arrived.
The duplication token was issued to PRICE SECURITY SERVICES.

levels.title: The Flooded Corridor
levels.objective: Restore the drainage controls to reach the service wing.

clue.title: A trail to the laundry
clue.text: The service corridor shows fresh drag marks leading towards the disused laundry rooms.

story_intro: The storm has flooded the corridor beyond the loading bay.
The drainage controls are here, but the power routing is broken.
A faded diagram shows the battery line feeding the pump controller.
story_reveal: The emergency pump starts. Water drains from the service passage.
Scuff marks run along the floor toward a locked laundry corridor.
Someone dragged a heavy load through here recently.

levels.title: The Archived Film
levels.objective: Put the four surviving 2019 camera records in chronological order.

clue.title: The driver in 2019
clue.text: Recovered records identify Daniel Price as the driver involved in Mara Ward’s fatal collision. Owen subsequently helped conceal it.

story_intro: A second copy of the 2019 footage survived on the old service archive.
Four timestamps. They cover the minutes around Mara’s death.
Rebuild the sequence before opening the images.
story_reveal: The sequence shows Daniel Price driving the motel company car. Mara walks along the shoulder.
The car strikes her. Daniel gets out, calls Owen, then moves the vehicle.
The original video is still damaged, but its sequence is clear.

levels.title: The Owner’s Ledger
levels.objective: Reorder payments to expose the recurring transfer pattern.

clue.title: Years of payments
clue.text: The motel’s ledger records repeated large October payments from Owen Mercer to Daniel Price’s business after the 2019 crash.

story_intro: Owen’s office contains a ledger marked SECURITY RETAINER.
Nina said the payments always happened after the yearly insurance review.
Someone’s mixed the entries. I’ll put the dates back in order.
story_reveal: Every October, Owen paid Daniel an unusually large “maintenance” fee.
He was paying to keep Daniel quiet.
Then Owen has been afraid of him for years.
A message arrives from Owen: “I’m at the front. Please, let me explain.”

levels.title: The Emergency Intercom
levels.objective: Reroute power to the emergency intercom outside the laundry.

clue.title: Nina is in the laundry
clue.text: Nina confirms she is locked behind the disused laundry door and names Daniel as her captor.

story_intro: Nina’s faint message came over the obsolete laundry intercom.
If I can make it transmit both ways, she might hear me.
The electrical switchboard still has an emergency supply.
story_reveal: Nina? If you can hear me, knock twice.
Two knocks carry through the wall.
Behind the laundry door... Daniel has the key... he’s coming back.
The line goes dead. Footsteps sound in the hall.

levels.title: The Contractor’s Case
levels.objective: Remove the case’s security plates to inspect the contents.

clue.title: Daniel’s cloning equipment
clue.text: Daniel Price’s case contains a card encoder and a duplicate NIGHT SHIFT credential, directly linking him to the forged access events.

story_intro: A contractor’s tool case is tucked behind the service switchboard.
Price Security Services. He left this where nobody would look.
The metal cover is secured with overlapping anti-tamper plates.
story_reveal: Inside are a programmable keycard writer, a second NIGHT SHIFT card and an empty evidence sleeve.
He used my cloned credential. And he’s still searching for Nina’s memory card.
The tool case also contains a laundry door override tag.

levels.title: The Only Explanation
levels.objective: Connect the three decisive pieces of evidence to the responsible person or act.

clue.title: Daniel identified
clue.text: The booking, duplicate credential and Nina’s testimony independently identify Daniel Price as the person who abducted her.

story_intro: Owen arrives, pale and dripping rainwater. Claire keeps her distance.
I hid what happened in 2019. That was my doing. But I didn’t take Nina.
Daniel. Nina found the old recording. He knew she’d shown Claire.
Before trusting him, assemble the physical evidence.
story_reveal: The records independently place Daniel behind the false booking, duplicate credential and abduction.
He thinks she has the only original footage. He locked her away until she tells him where it is.
We have the copy. But we still need Nina.
From the service hall comes a sharp metallic bang. The laundry lights go out.

levels.title: The Laundry Override
levels.objective: Use the maintenance override printed on the contractor tag.

clue.title: Laundry entrance unlocked
clue.text: The maintenance override opened the outer laundry door. Nina is still alive beyond the boiler room.

story_intro: 12:54 AM. You and Claire reach the disused laundry entrance.
The door’s electrified. I can hear someone inside.
Daniel’s tool case has an override tag. L-6421.
The keypad accepts the four digits after the L.
story_reveal: The outer door unlocks. A burst of hot air rolls through the opening.
We’re coming. Keep talking to us.

levels.title: The Boiler Bypass
levels.objective: Reconnect the isolation control so the pressure door can be opened safely.

clue.title: Safe access to the inner corridor
clue.text: The boiler was isolated, allowing access to the inner laundry corridor without opening a pressurised door.

story_intro: A steaming boiler blocks the inner corridor. The safety interlock has been bypassed.
The pressure door will stay sealed until the isolation valve gets power.
The diagram is still intact on the panel.
story_reveal: The isolation valve engages. Steam clears from the passage.
He told me he’d destroy everything if the police arrived.
We already backed up the card. Just stay away from the door.

levels.title: The Last Barrier
levels.objective: Rearrange the jammed lock segments to release the inner safety gate.

clue.title: Nina rescued
clue.text: Nina has been freed from the laundry. Daniel Price is still on the property and knows the evidence was recovered.

story_intro: The final gate is blocked by a damaged mechanical interlock.
These segments are out of position. The gate won’t release.
I can hear you. Daniel took my phone. Please don’t leave.
story_reveal: The gate slides free. Nina stumbles out, shaken but able to walk.
He wanted the card. I told him it was gone.
A door slams at the far end of the passage.

levels.title: The Original Frame
levels.objective: Rebuild the final undamaged video frame from the 2019 recording.

clue.title: The original frame
clue.text: The restored original video frame clearly identifies Daniel Price driving the car involved in Mara Ward’s fatal collision.

story_intro: Nina shows you a hidden duplicate of the last surviving camera frame.
I made another backup. Daniel was looking for the wrong card.
The one we found proves the timeline. This one can prove who was behind the wheel.
story_reveal: The repaired frame clearly shows Daniel Price behind the steering wheel of the company car.
That’s the first image of him they’ve ever let me see.
Send it to the police before he reaches the switchboard.

levels.title: The Emergency Uplink
levels.objective: Match the physical evidence feeds to the three emergency upload channels.

clue.title: Evidence preserved off-site
clue.text: The CCTV, duplicate-card audit and original 2019 frame have been transferred to the police evidence server.

story_intro: The police dispatcher is still connected on an emergency data link.
The upload board needs each file routed to the right channel.
I can shut this whole system down!
Match each evidence source to its secure destination.
story_reveal: Evidence received and time-stamped. Officers are entering the service road.
Footsteps race towards the switchboard. The backup screen remains green.
We’re staying here. The police are almost through the gate.

levels.title: The Final Account
levels.objective: Put the decisive six events into chronological order to complete the case statement.

clue.title: Case closed
clue.text: Nina was rescued; Daniel was detained; the recovered evidence exposed the 2019 collision, Owen’s cover-up, and the events at the motel.

story_intro: The dispatcher requests a final sequence of events while officers approach.
Confirm the chronology: the original death, the cover-up, and tonight’s abduction.
We have everything. The order will show how it all connects.
Reconstruct the six key events, from earliest to latest.
story_reveal: The statement is transmitted. Officers enter the laundry corridor and confront Daniel.
Suspect detained. We have Nina and two witnesses safe.
Mara spent seven years without anyone hearing the truth.
As morning breaks over the flooded coastline, investigators take Owen in for questioning about the cover-up.
The records are preserved. The investigation can now proceed without the motel controlling the story.
